cards.explanation: The answer is the narrow door, friends. Jesus says, “Make every effort to enter through the narrow door.” Someone asked Him for a number, and I think He handed back something to DO instead. That's one answer a calculator can't help with.
The answer is False. Jesus says, “For many, I tell you, will try to enter and will not be able.” So trying isn't the same as getting through, friends. That's why He tells them to make every effort.

The answer is “I do not know where you are from.” Once the door is shut and the knocking starts, the master of the house replies with that line. There's no morning appointment and no waiting room in what Jesus says. Just that one line, and then they get ready with their reasons.
The answer is evildoers, friends. The master says, “Depart from me, all you evildoers.” It's a heavy line. The knocking in verse 25 ends with this answer.

The answer is Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and all the prophets. Jesus says they will see “…Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets in the kingdom of God…” They see those faces while they themselves are thrown out. I think the weeping hits harder because those faces are right there in front of them.

The answer is all four directions, friends! Jesus says, “People will come from east and west and north and south…” That's a long guest list. East, west, north and south, and every one of them gets a seat at the table in the kingdom of God.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “…some who are last will be first, and some who are first will be last.” That's how He wraps up what He told them about the door and the table. It's a flip, and I think those listeners felt it.

The answer is True. Some Pharisees come to Jesus and say, “Leave this place and get away, because Herod wants to kill You.” That's a warning with a lot of weight on it. They don't beat around the bush.

The answer is driving out demons and healing people, friends. Jesus says, “…I will keep driving out demons and healing people today and tomorrow…” The warning doesn't change His plans. He just keeps working.
The answer is False, friends. Jesus says, “Nevertheless, I must keep going today and tomorrow and the next day…” He isn't waiting for the danger to pass. He keeps moving toward Jerusalem.

The answer is a hen gathering her chicks under her wings! Jesus says He has longed to gather Jerusalem's children together “…as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings…” It's a picture of a mother bird pulling her little ones in close. I think there's real tenderness in that.
The answer is False, and Jesus says it Himself. He says how often He longed to gather them, “…but you were unwilling!” He wanted to gather them, and they weren't willing. I hear sorrow in that.

The answer is “Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord.” Jesus says, “…you will not see Me again until you say, ‘Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord.’…” It's a line about welcoming Him. He ends on that note, and so does the passage.
